works.title: The Fundamental Laws of Supremacism and Egalitarianism
works.blurb: The axiomatic substrate of the framework: the Fundamental Law of Supremacism (sustained conflict necessarily implies a supremacist claim) and the Fundamental Law of Egalitarianism (fully maintained pairwise equality precludes sustained conflict), each demonstrated by proof by contradiction.

works.title: The Madisonian Separation of Powers Objective Compliance Test
works.blurb: Recovers Madison's actual framework and derives a six-step objective compliance test for separation-of-powers violations, validated against 36 Supreme Court decisions spanning 154 years (1872–2021) at a 100% correspondence rate.

works.title: Means, Not Views: The Constitutional Distinction Between Radicalism and Extremism
works.blurb: Identifies and defends the First Amendment distinction between radicalism (challenge through constitutional means) and extremism (use of unconstitutional means), drawn at means, not views — reading Brandenburg, Claiborne Hardware, and Snyder v. Phelps as the operative authorities.

works.title: Anchor and Bridge: A Three-Layer Architecture for Universal Deployment
works.blurb: Connects the Laws of Supremacism/Egalitarianism (substrate), the Means/Views distinction (operational vocabulary), and international human-rights frameworks (remedial channel) into a unified architecture for deploying the distinction in destinations of conventional extremism.

works.title: Applied Diagnostics: Structural Analysis of Active Conflicts
works.blurb: Applies the bodily-jurisdiction framework's seven-step diagnostic template to active conflicts, using a consistent case structure to enable cross-case comparison and pattern observation. The diagnostic operates symmetrically across parties.

works.title: Bodily Jurisdiction: The Floor of Constitutional Authority
works.blurb: Restates bodily autonomy structurally rather than as a balanceable right: the body is a sovereign jurisdictional sphere and the floor of the constitutional architecture, the primary sovereignty from which all higher-level authority is derivative.

works.title: Torture in the Codified Democratic Order: The May 2026 Sumud Flotilla
works.blurb: Uses the May 2026 Global Sumud Flotilla interception to demonstrate the three-level meta-violation structure of the codified democratic order and argues the conduct triggers mandatory universal jurisdiction under Article 7 of the Convention Against Torture.

works.title: The Rejection of Law: Treaty Defection, State Secession, and the Fractal Constitution
works.blurb: Argues that the principle forbidding state secession (Texas v. White) is structurally identical to the principle the Bolton 'unsigning' of the Rome Statute violates; selective enforcement — binding states downward while exempting the federal executive upward — is a particularized-enforcement violation.

works.title: The Declaration of Humanity: An Inclusive Definition and Its Operational Necessity
works.blurb: Shifts from assertion-form articulations of universal rights to a definitional-form premise — humanity is every person, family, people, and nation, without exception — which is invulnerable to the redescription mechanism through which regimes of organized exclusion operate.

works.title: The Ratification Protocol: A Two-Stage Architecture for Member Commitment
works.blurb: Operationalizes the Declaration of Humanity into a two-stage procedure (Member Commitment Declaration, grace period, certification, Full Ratification) by which polities affirm or restore membership in the codified democratic order while sovereignty is preserved at every stage.

works.title: The Board of Peace: An Operational Anatomy of USURPATION at the International Scale
works.blurb: Applies the corpus's diagnostic apparatus to the Board of Peace's formal instruments, finding a dual Power Separation Vulnerability — paradigm USURPATION by the Board paired with paradigm ABDICATION by the UN Security Council in Resolution 2803.

works.title: A Restorative Reading of Genesis 1–3
works.subtitle: The Creation Narrative in the Hebrew and Its Versions
works.blurb: Genesis 1–3 is one narrative told twice. The first telling gives the frame, six days and a rest; the second goes back over the sixth day and gives the detail. A reading of the Hebrew and of its versions, from the Septuagint to the King James, cited at the leaf for every reading.

works.title: The Subject's Unanswered Plea
works.subtitle: A Restorative and Comparative History of Immunity
works.blurb: The case that founded official immunity was a documented miscarriage of justice, a death by drowning recast as murder, a conviction on examinations taken down in a language the witnesses did not speak, and a court that answered the surviving kinsman’s sworn complaint against the trial judge by defacing it. Six Parts put the question the decree reserved to every order that has answered it, cited at the page.
